The native-over-Haar matching advantage is also observed in the descriptive exclusive-positive secondary (uncovered assignments, SAT formulas with no covered solution; matched axes may include published units; not multiplicity-controlled). This is a within-checkpoint, within-bank single-axis-separability comparison against Haar references whose exchangeability null is generically false for nonnegative sparse ReLU coordinates; it does not separate assignment-specific alignment from generic coordinate privilege (see the clause-presence and SAT/solution-count control gaps) and is not evidence that any coordinate is causally used.
